robot: a pair of I2RT YAM arms on 0.15 m risers at the back of a work table, each with a parallel gripper

frame.suite: the bench frame: origin on the table top at the middle of the table, +x right and +y away from the front camera, +z up
frame.base_text: midway between the two arms' bases, 0.15 m above the table top, at the back of the table: +X towards the front of the table (towards the front camera), +Y to the robot's left, +Z up; the table top is z = -0.15

ee.point: tool centre point: the pinch point between the finger pads (+z out of the hand, +y the direction the fingers close along)
ee.mode_text: the robot's own inverse kinematics, one control step at a time, along a straight line from the measured pose; no path planning, no collision checking

left.note: the arm the bench calls left: at bench x = -0.26, on the robot's right-hand side (base y = -0.26)

ee.point: tool centre point: the pinch point between the finger pads (+z out of the hand, +y the direction the fingers close along)
ee.mode_text: the robot's own inverse kinematics, one control step at a time, along a straight line from the measured pose; no path planning, no collision checking

right.note: the arm the bench calls right: at bench x = +0.26, on the robot's left-hand side (base y = +0.26)

signals_text: End the episode or talk to the operator; the note is the text (at most 2000 characters). Exits, each ends the episode at once and the robot stops where it is: done = the request is fulfilled (the note says what was done); infeasible = it cannot be carried out (the note says why); decline = it should not be carried out (the note says why). A request done in part ends with the exit that fits the part left undone, the note saying what was done and what was left. ask_operator = ask the operator a question; their answer comes back in this call's result (`operator`). report = tell the operator something, with category 0 incident, 1 hazard or 2 note; the operator reads reports as they arrive, while an exit's note may be read much later, so anything the operator has to act on belongs in a report. ask_operator and report take no robot time.
notes: The robot base frame of these tools: origin midway between the two arms' bases on their 0.15 m risers, bench (0, 0.26, 0.15); +X towards the front of the table (bench -y), +Y to the robot's left (bench +x), +Z up. The table top is z = -0.15 and the middle of the table is at (0.26, 0, -0.15). The arms keep the bench's names, which are as the front camera sees them: `left` stands at bench x = -0.26, which is the robot's right-hand side (base y = -0.26), and `right` at base y = +0.26. A hand pointing straight down with its fingers closing along the base's Y axis is quaternion_wxyz (0, 1, 0, 0). Goals for both arms in one call move them together. The robot's own spec (describe_robot spec_file) and its camera poses use the bench frame: origin on the table top at the middle of the table, +x to the right and +y away from the viewer as the front camera sees it, +z up. An end-effector goal is followed by the robot's own inverse kinematics, one control step at a time, on a straight line from the measured pose at about 0.15 m/s unless duration_s is given; nothing plans a way or avoids anything, so the hand and the arm can run into things and people. A pose the arm cannot reach is approached as near as its joints allow. A motion is not interrupted once it has started: keep motions short where people or things move. Time passes only inside calls. Gripper: a value below 0.5 opens the fingers fully, 0.5 or more closes them fully; on a thing the fingers stop where they meet it and, once both pads rest on it, the hand holds it. Every move keeps the gripper as it reads now: open while the fingers are open, else fully closed. Change the gripper in a goal of its own: given together with a pose it changes gradually during the motion. For a partial opening or a gentle grip send execute_trajectory space native rows (joint_position: the joints then the gripper; ee_pose: x y z qw qx qy qz gripper in the bench frame; gripper 0 open .. 1 closed, a position target of the fingers). gripper_opening_m is the free distance between the pads; describe_robot's spec_file has the table from gripper command to opening. Messages that reach the robot come back in `messages` of any result; the operator's answer to ask_operator comes back in `operator`. The only free text you send is a signal's note. Camera intrinsics (K) and poses are in describe_robot's spec_file: world_from_cam in the bench frame for the fixed cameras, tcp_from_cam (in the frame of the tool centre point) for a wrist camera.
